parsed.explanation: Private same-sex conduct is legal and no trans-specific offence, screening, facilities, custody or care rule is documented, so there is no capital or routine-sweep regime. If outed, however, a visitor faces entrenched societal discrimination, taboo/imported framing, concealment, no anti-discrimination recourse and no LGR, plus a public-morals offence punishable by 6 months-2 years (2-5 years where a child is involved). Documented false-accusation arrests and law-enforcement mistreatment/torture of LGBTQ people, in a general impunity and harsh-prison context, make detention a severe, unremedied exposure. Thin trans-specific data resolves downward, not to safety.

entry_documents.exposure: No legal gender recognition; visitor assessed against documents as issued and relationship may be read as same-sex by birth-sex status.
entry_documents.protection: Not documented. No evidence foreign documents, X markers or mismatches are accepted without questioning.
entry_documents.interaction: Document assessment can interact with Article 85 public-morals enforcement if presentation or a partner is read as same-sex.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: Documented arrests on false same-sex accusations and mistreatment/torture of LGBTQ people by law enforcement; 2012 general record of torture, extrajudicial killings and harsh prisons with impunity.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented. No trans visitor custody, placement, screening or consular-access protection documented.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Any public-affection or false-accusation arrest leads into a custodial system with documented abuse and no documented remedy.

care_services.exposure: Documented discrimination in healthcare and employment; no anti-discrimination law in health, employment, education or services; sensitive-data protection covers sexual orientation, not gender identity.
care_services.protection: Not documented for trans visitor care continuity, emergency placement or confidentiality.
care_services.interaction: Healthcare disclosure can out a visitor in a setting with documented discrimination and no legal recourse.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: Article 85 punishes public same-sex expression of love with 6 months-2 years or fine, heavier than other morals offences; SOGI issues taboo, framed as imported and contrary to values.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Private consenting adult conduct is legal; 2012 report recorded no arrests under the provisions, but current enforcement data is not documented.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: The public/private line is the operative exposure; visibility or accusation can move a visitor from lawful private conduct to arrest.

minors_guardians.exposure: Where a child is involved in public same-sex expression, adult faces 2-5 years; marriage constitutionally man-woman, no recognition for a relationship read as same-sex by birth sex.
minors_guardians.protection: Not documented for travelling families, guardianship, school or care of a minor.
minors_guardians.interaction: Travelling with a minor raises the Article 85 penalty tier and family-recognition exposure beyond an adult travelling alone.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Entrenched societal discrimination against LGBT people, concealment to avoid it, maintaining a relationship described as dangerous; police mistreatment documented.
street_violence_police_response.protection: 2023 report recorded no violence reports, but whether incidents were absent or unreported is unresolved; no trans-specific tolerance documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Social hostility plus police as documented perpetrators, not protector, leaves street exposure without documented response.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: No anti-discrimination law, no known LGBTQ-rights organisations documented, no conversion-therapy ban; UPR recommendations and UN statement signing are not shown to operate as recourse.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Not documented. Data-protection prohibition on sexual-orientation processing does not address gender identity.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Paper commitments do not offset documented arrests, torture allegations and discrimination where no working remedy is documented.

anchor_checks.comparison: Similar police harassment, discretion and weak courts, but this case is lower: Article 85 carries imprisonment and law-enforcement torture is documented, with entrenched discrimination and no recourse, whereas 0.35-B detention rarely becomes imprisonment.

Similar birth-sex document assessment, short custodial exposure, slow/ineffective remedies and no execution, but this case lacks documented trans-specific prison placement or raids; its documented risk is via the public-morals law and LGBTQ police abuse, so it sits near this anchor.

Higher than this anchor: 0.55-B is mainly administrative delay, refusal and slow appeal without credible imprisonment, while this dossier documents imprisonment-eligible charges, police torture and societal hostility with no working remedy.

Higher than this anchor: no documented routine arrest of visitors for presentation, months of pretrial beating as standard practice, or capital provision for presentation; private conduct is legal and 2012 enforcement was recorded as nil, though current data is missing.

parsed.synthesis: Combined regime: lawful private conduct sits beside an imprisonment-eligible public-morals offence enforced at least by false-accusation arrests, with documented police mistreatment/torture, harsh impunity-era detention, entrenched discrimination and no anti-discrimination, LGR, facilities, custody or care protections. No trans-specific facilities, screening or violence data is documented, so severity is extrapolated from the LGBTQ-collective record. That yields severe, unremedied exposure if outed, especially with a minor, without the organised targeting or capital pathway of the lowest anchors.
